spine: 1. 一支文字偵測器跑過 arXiv 論文，報出「32% 疑似 AI 代寫」，比前 ChatGPT 時代 0.4% 的控制組基準高了約 80 倍。
2. 這個門檻是刻意設定的操作點：讓 0.4% 的前 LLM 論文誤報，代價是漏抓 15% 真正的 AI 學術文字——不是讀心術，是一個統計選擇。
3. 按領域拆開，數字從電腦科學的 65.0% 一路掉到數學的 0.7%，橫跨十個領域組、12,750 篇論文的樣本。
4. 候選解釋一：數學論文真的很少用 AI——數學自己的 2021–2022 控制年基準是 0%，不支持「偵測器對數學文字系統性誤判」這個反方向的懷疑。
5. 候選解釋二：數學論文的寫法本身讓偵測器失靈——公式與證明結構占滿全文，拿掉公式後剩下的散文對偵測器來說「分布外」，不像它訓練時見過的科學英文。
6. 作者自己承認：這兩個解釋在現有資料裡無法分開，0.7% 這種低分，究竟是採用率低的證據，還是偵測器看不懂的證據，論文給不出答案。
7. 但不是所有數字都一樣脆弱——電腦科學的 65.0% 遠高於任何合理的雜訊地板，這個結論穩固；數學、天文物理這類低分領域，才是「只能讀成下限、不能讀成事實」的地方。

perspective.mechanism: A text detector is calibrated against a known-human 2021-2022 control corpus by fixing the decision threshold so exactly 0.4% of control papers trip it, then measuring recall (85%) against known-AI academic text at that same threshold. Applying the threshold to unlabeled recent papers yields a 'flagged share' that mixes genuine AI-written text with a small, field-specific false-positive floor.
perspective.tradeoff: A stricter threshold eliminates false positives but misses more real AI-written text (lower recall), and vice versa; the study fixed one operating point (0.4% FPR / 85% recall) as an editorial choice. Any field whose reported percentage sits close to that floor is statistically fragile, while fields far above the floor (CS at 65%) are robust to the choice of operating point.
perspective.reader_use: An engineer evaluating any AI-detection claim should ask for the calibration operating point (FPR/recall) and check whether it was measured on the same text register being classified. A low score in an out-of-distribution register (dense notation, sparse prose) is weak evidence of absence, not proof of absence.

notes.quote: at a 0.4% false-positive rate it clears 99.6% of genuine pre-LLM scientific text and recovers 85% of AI academic text
notes.interpretation: The detector's calibrated operating point: 0.4% false-positive rate on known-human pre-LLM text, 85% recall on known-AI academic text. This is the single operating point the whole study's thresholding rests on.

notes.quote: climbs in two waves to about 32% over the most recent complete quarter, peaking near 39% in early 2026
notes.interpretation: Headline current flagged share (~32%) and peak (~39%, early 2026). Both are aggregate-across-fields figures, not field-specific.

notes.quote: Computer science leads at about 65%. Mathematics is lowest, near 0.7%
notes.interpretation: The two extremes of the field-level spread, used as anchor examples throughout the post.

notes.quote: We sampled ten field groups, roughly 25 papers per field per month, from January 2023 to July 2026, plus eight control months across 2021 and 2022, for 12,750 papers in total.
notes.interpretation: Full methodology: sample composition, cadence, and total N. Grounds all sample-size claims in the post's intro.

notes.quote: Mathematics papers are dominated by notation and theorem-proof structure, and once equations and references are removed the remaining prose is sparse
notes.interpretation: The mechanical reason mathematics text is out-of-distribution for a detector trained on general scientific English prose.

notes.quote: The result is consistent with two very different explanations, lower adoption or reduced detector sensitivity in that register, and this data cannot separate them.
notes.interpretation: The core admitted ambiguity that drives the whole investigation: the authors explicitly say their own data cannot resolve adoption vs. blind-spot for low-scoring fields.

notes.quote: lifts off within months of ChatGPT, and climbs in two waves to about 32%
notes.interpretation: Qualitative shape of the timeline: rapid onset tied to ChatGPT's release, then a two-wave climb. No month-by-month intermediate values are given.

notes.quote: the reported prevalence is a lower bound: the true share is at least what we measured
notes.interpretation: Explicit epistemic framing: every reported percentage should be read as a floor, not a precise point estimate.
Computer science row of the results table: control-year baseline 0.2%, flagged 65.0%, 95% CI [59.3, 70.3].

notes.quote: Quantitative biology | 3.5% | 56.3% | [51.0, 61.7]
notes.interpretation: Quantitative biology row: control-year baseline 3.5% (notably higher than the 0.4% overall calibration target), flagged 56.3%, 95% CI [51.0, 61.7].
Astrophysics row: control-year baseline 0.0%, flagged 10.7%, 95% CI [7.3, 14.3].
Mathematics row: control-year baseline 0.0%, flagged 0.7%, 95% CI [0.0, 1.7]. The lowest flagged field, and the post's central puzzle case.
The remaining six field-group rows of the results table, used in full in the post's comparison table.

notes.quote: set the flag threshold so that exactly 0.4% of them trip it.
notes.interpretation: Confirms the threshold-setting procedure: 0.4% is a deliberately chosen calibration target against the pre-LLM control corpus, not an incidental measurement.

notes.quote: the per-field control levels are only approximate
notes.interpretation: Explicit caveat on the per-field control column used in the results table — not a precise calibration, used to hedge the table's control-baseline column in the post.

notes.quote: Every reported figure carries a bootstrap 95% confidence interval.
notes.interpretation: Confirms the CI figures used throughout the results table are bootstrap 95% intervals.

notes.quote: The control column is each field's 2021 to 2022 flag rate averaged over three sensitivity settings
notes.interpretation: Defines what the 'control' column in the results table actually measures: each field's own pre-LLM flag rate, averaged across three sensitivity settings.

notes.quote: A mathematics paper drafted with heavy model assistance may score low because its prose is out of distribution for the detector, so a low score in mathematics is weak evidence that a human wrote the paper.
notes.interpretation: The authors' own statement of the detector-blind-spot hypothesis for mathematics, explicitly framed as making a low math score 'weak evidence' rather than disproof.

notes.quote: in the low-scoring fields the ranking should be read as a lower bound on adoption.
notes.interpretation: Direct instruction from the authors on how to read low-scoring fields: as a floor on adoption, not a point estimate.

notes.quote: Methodology · 5 min read · 2026
notes.interpretation: Only the publication year (2026) is recoverable from the byline; no specific month/day is given, so published date is recorded as null.

notes.quote: We scored the full body text instead of the abstract
notes.interpretation: 研究團隊評分時取整篇內文而非只掃摘要

notes.quote: we have seen the same paper score under 20% on its abstract and over 70% on its body.
notes.interpretation: 同一篇論文摘要可低於 20%、內文卻高於 70%

notes.quote: we pulled the version-1 PDF, so a paper revised in 2026 cannot leak modern text back into its 2023 slot.
notes.interpretation: 只抓第一版 PDF，避免改版把現代文本洩漏回舊年份的時間格

notes.quote: a single score is never grounds to accuse a specific person.
notes.interpretation: 單一分數不足以指控特定個人

claims.claim_text: 整體疑似 AI 代筆的比例落在 32% 左右，最高在 2026 年初一度衝上 39%，而 2021 到 2022 那批「前 ChatGPT」控制組，這個比例穩穩地卡在 0.4%
claims.location: 開場段 / H2「32%，而且沒有天花板」

claims.note: Headline 32%/39% match n02 verbatim; the 0.4% control floor matches the threshold-setting procedure (n14). Post uses '約/一度' hedging consistent with source's 'about/near'.

claims.claim_text: 研究團隊把門檻設在「讓 2021 到 2022 年的論文剛好有 0.4% 會觸發」的位置，同一個門檻拿去測已知是 AI 寫的學術文字，抓到 85%
claims.evidence: at a 0.4% false-positive rate it clears 99.6% of genuine pre-LLM scientific text and recovers 85% of AI academic text; set the flag threshold so that exactly 0.4% of them trip it.
claims.note: Both the 0.4% FPR calibration target and the 85% recall figure match n01/n14 verbatim. Post asserts, source asserts.

claims.claim_text: 控制年份（2021 到 2022）平穩落在 0.4%，ChatGPT 問世後數月內開始起飛，接著分兩波爬升，來到近期完整季度的約 32%，2026 年初一度衝上約 39% 的高點
claims.evidence: lifts off within months of ChatGPT, and climbs in two waves to about 32%; climbs in two waves to about 32% over the most recent complete quarter, peaking near 39% in early 2026
claims.note: Timeline shape (lift-off within months of ChatGPT, two-wave climb to ~32%, ~39% peak) matches n07+n02 verbatim.

claims.claim_text: 報告沒有拆解每一波背後對應的是哪些新工具或新版本，合理的推測是，這條線接下來還會有第三波、第四波，而不是已經摸到頂了

claims.location: H2「候選解釋一」/ 表格 widget
claims.note: All four field flagged-shares and their 95% CIs match the results-table rows verbatim.

claims.location: H2「候選解釋一」/ 表格 widget
claims.note: All six middle-field flagged-shares match n13 verbatim; CIs in the widget table also match.

claims.claim_text: 數學這一欄是 0.0%，天文物理也是 0.0%，電腦科學是 0.2%，量化生物學則明顯偏高，落在 3.5%

claims.evidence: Quantitative biology | 3.5% | ...; set the flag threshold so that exactly 0.4% of them trip it.
claims.note: 3.5% is the highest control baseline in the table (verified against all ten rows). '將近九倍' is the post's arithmetic (3.5/0.4 = 8.75), correctly derived from sourced numbers.

claims.claim_text: 報告裡每個領域都附了自己的「控制年基準」——用 2021 到 2022 年、三種靈敏度設定平均出來的誤判率

claims.claim_text: 報告也提醒，這一欄的控制基準只是近似值，不是精確校準，讀的時候不能當成沒有誤差的定值

claims.claim_text: 報告裡的每一個百分比，都附了 bootstrap 重抽樣算出來的 95% 信賴區間

claims.evidence: Every reported figure carries a bootstrap 95% confidence interval.
claims.note: Matches n16 verbatim.

claims.claim_text: 報告裡明講的 85% 召回率，是在「一般學術文字」上量出來的整體數字，並沒有針對數學論文單獨測過
claims.evidence: at a 0.4% false-positive rate it clears 99.6% of genuine pre-LLM scientific text and recovers 85% of AI academic text; The result is consistent with two very different explanations, lower adoption or reduced detector sensitivity in that register, and this data cannot separate them.
claims.note: The load-bearing part (85% recall is a general figure on AI academic text) matches n01 verbatim. The negative rider ('not separately measured on mathematics') is not a literal source sentence, but is a reasonable reading of the source's generic framing and is exactly the ambiguity n06 admits; source does not contradict it. Accepted as verified.

claims.claim_text: 數學論文被公式與定理證明結構占滿，拿掉公式和引用之後，剩下的散文非常稀疏，跟偵測器訓練時看過的科學英文不一樣……它的散文對偵測器來說「分布外」(out of distribution)
claims.evidence: Mathematics papers are dominated by notation and theorem-proof structure, and once equations and references are removed the remaining prose is sparse and unlike the scientific English the detector was trained on; ...its prose is out of distribution for the detector
claims.note: n05 is a verbatim TRUNCATION of a longer source sentence; the full sentence (re-fetched) ends '...sparse and unlike the scientific English the detector was trained on', which supplies the post's '跟偵測器訓練時看過的科學英文不一樣'. 'out of distribution' matches n18 verbatim. Fully supported.

claims.claim_text: 一篇大量借助模型輔助寫成的數學論文，分數可能偏低……數學論文拿到低分，只是「人類寫的」的薄弱證據，不是強證據
claims.evidence: A mathematics paper drafted with heavy model assistance may score low because its prose is out of distribution for the detector, so a low score in mathematics is weak evidence that a human wrote the paper.
claims.note: Source is hedged ('may score low', 'weak evidence'); post preserves the hedge ('可能偏低', '薄弱證據，不是強證據'). hedge_delta none — no inflation.

claims.claim_text: 他們自己寫下的結論是，這個結果同時符合兩種截然不同的解釋：採用率真的偏低，或者偵測器在這種文字風格裡敏感度下降，而現有的資料沒辦法把兩者分開

Calling it 'the average of the ten fields' is the author's characterization of an across-field aggregate; the arithmetic mean of the ten field rows is ~33.4%, close to the reported 32% aggregate, so the characterization is fair and not misleading for the post's 'averages hide the spread' argument. No action.
